decision_conditions: The proposal is considered unacceptable in principle, introducing two dwellings in a sensitive backland location that fails to comply with the criteria of Policy DMH 6 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020). The development, by reason of its scale, massing and loss of landscaped curtilage, would result in an incongruous and uncharacteristic form of intensification, eroding the openness and verdant setting of the site. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policy DMH 6 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020).

The proposal, by reason of its siting, scale, massing and design, including prominent rear dormers, would inappropriately intensify and subdivide the rear curtilage of the Grade II listed Old Barn House. It would cause less than substantial harm to the setting of the listed building (moderate-to-high level) and to the character and appearance of the Eastcote Village Conservation Area, without adequate heritage gain or public benefits to outweigh this harm. The development would also appear incongruous and overly dominant within this sensitive backland location, detracting from the established character of the area. The proposal is therefore contrary to Sections 16 and 66 of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990, paragraphs 138 and 140 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), Policy HC1 of the London Plan (2021), Policy HE1 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012), and Policies DMHB 1, DMHB 2, DMHB 4, DMHB 11 and DMHB 12 of the Hillingdon Local Plan

The proposal involves the removal of 10 trees, including five Category B specimens, which make a positive contribution to the setting of the Grade II listed Old Barn House and the character of the Eastcote Village Conservation Area. No arboricultural justification has been provided for their removal, and the replacement planting proposed is inadequate in both number and quality, failing to compensate for the loss. The development would therefore result in adverse and irreversible impacts to trees, landscaping, and the verdant character of the site, detrimental to visual amenity, the setting of the listed building, and the Conservation Area. The proposal is contrary to paragraph 136 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2023), Policy G7 of the London Plan (2021), and Policies DMHB 4, DMHB 11, DMHB 12 and DMHB 14 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 2 (2020).

The application fails to demonstrate that the loss of established on-plot parking spaces serving the 'host' office based use would not have an adverse parking impact on the local highway network thereby potentially leading to adverse congestion/additional on-street parking to the detriment of pedestrian and highway safety contrary to Local Plan: Part 2 Development Management Plan (2020) Policies DMT 1 & DMT 2 and Policy T4 of the London Plan (2021).

The application site lies in close proximity to dense woodland and a watercourse, providing suitable habitats for protected species including bats, badgers, owls and other wildlife. The proposal involves the removal of 10 trees and associated vegetation, which would further reduce habitat availability. The application is not supported by a Preliminary Ecological Appraisal, bat survey or any ecological assessment. In the absence of this information, and given the reasonable likelihood of protected species being present, the Council cannot be satisfied that the development would avoid or mitigate harm to biodiversity or habitats. The proposal is therefore contrary to paragraph 188 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2024), Policy G6 of the London Plan (2021), and Policy DMEI 7 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020).

The proposal fails to demonstrate through a satisfactory Fire Safety Strategy how the development would achieve the highest standards of fire safety in terms of design, means of escape, firefighting access and risk reduction. In the absence of this information, the Council cannot be satisfied that the development would provide a safe and resilient environment for future occupiers. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policy D12 of the London Plan (2021) and paragraph 188 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2024).

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to all relevant planning legislation, regulations, guidance, circulars and Council policies, including The Human Rights Act (1998) (HRA 1998) which makes it unlawful for the Council to act incompatibly with Convention rights, specifically Article 6 (right to a fair hearing); Article 8 (right to respect for private and family life); Article 1 of the First Protocol (protection of property) and Article 14 (prohibition of discrimination).

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to the policies and proposals in the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012) and Part 2 (2020) set out below, including Supplementary Planning Guidance, and to all relevant material considerations, including The London Plan (2021) and national guidance.

This is a reminder that Under the terms of the Planning Act 2008 (as amended) and Community Infrastructure Levy Regulations 2010 (as amended), should an application for appeal be allowed, the proposed development would be deemed as 'chargeable development' and therefore liable to pay the London Borough of Hillingdon Community Infrastructure Levy (CIL) and the Mayor of London's Community Infrastructure Levy (CIL). This would be calculated in accordance with the London Borough of Hillingdon CIL Charging Schedule 2014 and the Mayor of London's CIL Charging Schedule 2012.
For more information on CIL matters please visit the planning portal page at: www.planningportal.gov.uk/planning/applications/howtoapply/whattosubmit/cil
description: Erection of two semi-detached dwellinghouses with associated parking and landscaping.
